2.text: before their eyes. Taking off my breeches, I stand on the ground without

3.text: any precautions. My buttocks have three eyes, and they keep watch for me.

4.text: They see every hidden keˊlᴇ, and they make the keˊlᴇ’s eyes to close. The

5.text: foremost reindeer I make very slow, using the two legs of the small pintail

6.text: duck, forked in two from its buttocks. Everything difficult to smell of I am

7.text: using all the time. I enter the confines of every place without any precaution.

8.text: I may sleep without care. All game have a liking for me; every kind of

9.text: game has a great love for me. Thus I have almost acquired a good careless

10.text: sleep. The thing lying under my pillow I have for my protector. Blowing

11.text: over it, I make it rebound backwards. I make it scatter downwards. The end.

15.text: When the hunters, having gone out in a boat, have found a herd of

16.text: walrus sleeping on the ice, and the boat makes a noise striking against the

17.text: small ice around, the man who practises the incantation says, “O walrus! I

18.text: put your ears on a broad iron pan, lest you should be able to hear the

19.text: rapping noise.” Then the hunters are able to approach, and kill all of the herd.

20.text: Told by Wɪyêˊnto (man) at Mariinsky Post, 1900.

22.text: (a) I am crying to the Zenith, straight windward. “Old woman, scrape

23.text: the sky all over with your little copper butchering-knife! A huk! You

24.text: have great breasts. I beat my hands three times, then I fall backward. I

25.text: put my left mitten on my right hand.” The end.

26.text: Told by Rɪteˊhrew (man) in the village Chikaˊyeva,

28.text: (b) “Western Wind, look here! Look down on my buttocks. We are

29.text: going to give you some fat. Cease blowing!” (The man pronouncing the

30.text: incantation lets his breeches fall down, and bucks leeward, exposing his bare

31.text: buttocks to the wind. At every word he claps his hands.)

32.text: Told by Aˊnɪqai (man) in Mariinsky Post, 1900.

33.text: 5. INCANTATIONS AGAINST THE COMING OF KEˊLET.

34.text: (a) When evening comes, I tie up two big bears, one on either side of

35.text: my entrance, and I speak thus: “You are so big and strong! At your side,

36.text: nothing ill can befall me.” If the keˊlet try to enter, the bears would catch
